item.title: Netanyahu’s speech at UN spurs protests in New York City: ‘Let Gaza live’
item.description:
A mass walkout of delegates before Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ’s address to the United Nations General Assembly prompted a fiery response from the Israeli leader. As Netanyahu took the stage, dozens of delegates from across the globe could be seen streaming out of the chamber in New York City. Chants of protest could also be heard in the hall as the U.N. president called the assembly to order. After taking the stage, Netanyahu said, "Before I begin, just a quick announcement, if there are any other moral cowards who haven't yet left this hall, please do so now," as cheers erupted from the remaining delegates in the chamber. item.title: Live: Pope heads to France on first state visit in 18 years
item.description:
Pope Leo XIV flies to France on Friday for the Vatican's first state visit to the European nation in 18 years, with artificial intelligence and young believers near the top of his agenda. President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte will be on the tarmac to greet the 71-year-old pope. Follow our liveblog for all the latest updates.

item.title: Netanyahu defends Israeli military action as delegates walk out before UN speech
item.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was on the defensive when he took the stage at the United Nations General Assembly on Thursday. His country is facing growing condemnation from all sides: In September, 11 European countries and Canada announced a joint plan to sanction Israel’s West Bank settlements , and in 62 percent of Americans report a negative opinion of his government in a recent Pew poll ; Netanyahu himself faces an International Criminal Court arrest warrant for war crimes including genocide. Protesters blocked streets outside hours before Netanyahu took the podium, and within the UN chamber, half of Netanyahu’s audience walked out before his speech even began. item.title: EU says Trump’s plan to ban US diesel exports would ‘negatively impact both sides’
item.description:
Demand for rail freight shipping is up, as trucking becomes more expensive. Both use diesel fuel, but trains are more efficient at carrying heavy loads long distances. Scott Olson/Getty Images Diesel fuel powers long-distance trucks, freight locomotives, boats and barges, farm machinery, construction and mining equipment, and backup generators. Its concentrated energy powers efficient engines that can haul heavy loads and refuel machines quickly . Those are all excellent attributes for long periods of heavy work on the move or in locations not connected to the electricity grid. So when diesel prices hit record highs, as they have, that increases the costs of essentials like food, transportation and even other energy sources. item.title: Thousands Rally Against Trump’s Kennedy Center Takeover
item.description:
President Trump’s mindset when it comes to the Kennedy Center is that of an authoritarian toddler: If he can’t have the toys he wants, he’ll try to break them and make sure no one else can have them, either. Thousands of furious DC-area residents and Kennedy Center patrons gathered in front of the arts center last week in protest of the president’s threats to tear the building down if he’s not allowed to inscribe his own name on its exterior. Thousands of people gathered outside the Kennedy Center last week to protest Trump’s takeover. item.title: Oil prices jump after Yemen’s Houthis claim attacks on Saudi facilities
item.description:
Saudi Arabia intercepted Houthi ballistic missiles on Thursday after warning several regions, including Mecca, of possible attacks. France said it would send military assets to help protect the Saudi oil terminal at Yanbu. The strikes came amid renewed fighting in Yemen that has killed dozens, according to sources cited by AFP.
